title: Executive Assistant
company: Dynamite Recruitment Solutions Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Executive Assistant

Location: Southampton
Salary: £40,000 per annum
Hours: Monday to Friday, 37.5 hours per week
Contract: Temp-to-Perm, with an opportunity to become permanent for the right candidate

We are looking for an experienced Executive Assistant/Personal Assistant to join a well-established and highly regarded organisation within the marine industry.

The successful candidate will be supporting senior directors and playing an important role within the day-to-day running of the organisation. Personality and cultural fit are particularly important, and we are looking for someone who is warm, approachable, professional and genuinely enjoys working closely with people.

Key Responsibilities
- Providing high-level administrative and organisational support to senior directors
- Managing diaries, meetings and appointments
- Coordinating meetings and ensuring actions and follow-ups are managed effectively
- Preparing documents, correspondence and reports
- Handling confidential and sensitive information with discretion
- Liaising with internal teams, clients and external contacts
- Helping to coordinate the smooth running of day-to-day activities
- Managing competing priorities and ensuring deadlines are met
- Acting as a reliable and trusted point of contact for the directors
- Supporting with general administrative and organisational tasks as required

You will ideally be:
- Have a background in an Executive/Personal Assistant role
- Warm, personable and approachable
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail
- Proactive and able to anticipate what needs to be done
- Confident communicating with people at all levels
- Discreet and trustworthy when handling confidential information
- Calm under pressure and able to manage competing priorities
- A strong team player who enjoys being part of a close-knit working environment
- Someone who takes ownership and can be relied upon to get things done

If you're an experienced EA or PA looking for a long-term opportunity where your personality, organisation and ability to build strong relationships will be genuinely valued, we'd love to hear from you.

Please apply with your CV today.

title: Front of House Coordinator
company: University Of Southampton Students Union - Agency - Permanent
description:
Job Title: Front of House Coordinator

Location: Southampton

Salary: Grade 3 - £28,303-£29,339 per annum

Job type: Full Time, Permanent

The Role:
As Front of House Coordinator, you will lead the day-to-day delivery of SUSU's reception service, room and event bookings, and Safety Bus and minibus operations. You will supervise and develop staff, coordinate rotas and operational cover, maintain effective systems and procedures, and work closely with internal teams, students, customers and external partners to provide a welcoming, efficient and high-quality service.

About You:
We are looking for an organised and approachable individual with experience in a senior administrative, business support or front-of-house role.
- You will have experience delivering excellent customer service and coordinating room bookings, events, or activities
- You will have experience supervising staff, managing rotas, and developing efficient systems and procedures to support service delivery
- You will have knowledge of basic financial processes, including quotes, invoicing and timesheets, alongside an understanding of health and safety, equality, diversity and inclusion, and sustainability
- As a confident communicator and proactive problem-solver, you will be comfortable managing competing priorities, working independently and identifying opportunities to improve services and enhance the customer experience
- You will have the flexibility to work across our operating hours, including early mornings, evenings and weekends

Most importantly, you will share our commitment to providing an excellent experience for students, staff, and visitors, and delivering high-quality services across the Students' Union.

About Us:
We are the University of Southampton Students' Union (SUSU) - independent from the University and run by students, for students. Our vision is simple: SUSU is here to enrich the life of every student. We are a workplace that's buzzing with life, ideas, and opportunities - where your work directly shapes the student experience.

As part of our team, you'll enjoy:
- Salary of £28,303-£29,339 per annum
- Generous paid holiday - 24 days per year, plus eight closure days (around Easter, August and Christmas) on top of eight bank holidays (and an opportunity to purchase up to an additional week of holiday).
- Great pension - we contribute 10% into your defined contributions pension scheme.
- Travel perks - discounted UniLink and Blue Star bus passes, a Cycle-to-Work scheme.

Apply Now:
Please use your cover letter to explain why you are interested in joining SUSU and demonstrate how your experience meets the requirements of the role. We would particularly like to hear about occasions when you have led or supported a team, delivered excellent customer service, coordinated bookings or operational activity, and improved a system or process. Please include specific examples and the positive outcomes you achieved.

You can easily apply using your CV and covering letter by clicking on 'Apply Now'.

To know before applying:

Closing Date: Midday, Friday 25 September (Please note that should a high volume of applications be received, the advert may close early, so we would encourage you to apply as soon as possible).

Interview Date: Thursday 8 October.

Regretfully, SUSU is NOT a sponsoring organisation and is, therefore, not able to sponsor you for a visa if you require one (such as Tier 2) to work in the UK.

Please note feedback will not be provided if you are not shortlisted for interview.

SUSU is an equal opportunities employer that values a diverse workforce and we want to reflect the student body that we represent. We value diversity, promote equality and challenge discrimination and will ensure that our recruitment activities are mindful of equality and diversity matters.

Candidates with the relevant experience or job titles of: Front of House Coordinator, Front of House Manager, Front of House Supervisor, Senior Front of House Coordinator, Customer Service Coordinator, Customer Service Supervisor, Customer Service Manager, Reception Coordinator, Reception Manager, Reception Supervisor, Receptionist, Senior Receptionist, Guest Services Coordinator, Guest Services Supervisor, may also be considered for this role.

title: Patient Administrator
description: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is delighted to offer a fantastic opportunity to work with us. Please see below for detailed job description of the role. Do you thrive in a fast-paced environment? Are you passionate about delivering exceptional administrative support that enhances the patient experience and journey? We are seeking a range of Patient Administrators, Patient Services Centre Administrators and Ward Secretaries to join our Trust. These roles are essential to the seamless operation of our services and have a significant impact on our patients' experiences. Your responsibilities will be varied and include direct communication with patients and healthcare professionals, coordinating appointment bookings, managing correspondence and actions from outpatient clinics, and ensuring the smooth flow of information between clinicians and support services. UHS offers outstanding training and development opportunities to help you achieve your career aspirations. Supporting the growth of our staff is fundamental to delivering high-quality, safe, and effective care. We provide a nurturing environment for professional development, and internal applicants looking to gain experience in different roles or areas of the hospital may be considered for secondment opportunities. Positions are available at Southampton General Hospital, Adanac Park, Royal South Hants Hospital, Princess Anne Hospital, and Lymington Hospital. There are several different Band 3 Administrator roles throughout the Trust that you may be allocated to. Below is a brief description of the main responsibilities of these roles. Ward Secretary This is an excellent opportunity for an organised individual with attention to detail and proficiency in Microsoft Office, who is eager to collaborate with various nursing professionals and the wider multidisciplinary team (MDT). Full-time and part-time positions are available. Main Responsibilities: Collaborate closely with ward leaders to provide administrative support in cancer care. Prepare documentation, communicate with stakeholders, and use Microsoft 365 to organise and schedule meetings on behalf of the Line Manager. Deliver exceptional customer service by providing a professional telephone service, taking accurate messages, and offering information and guidance as appropriate. Patient Administrator We are looking for highly motivated and proactive individuals to join our busy department as Patient Administrators. In this role, you will build strong relationships with consultants, administrative teams, nursing staff, and external providers, ensuring a smooth patient pathway through the department. Strong written and verbal communication skills, along with the ability to work both independently and as part of a team, are essential. You will also provide cross-cover for other administrators to maintain consistent and effective administration services. Working closely with your team of consultants, your duties will vary but will include direct communication with patients and healthcare professionals, arranging appointments, managing correspondence from outpatient clinics, and facilitating the flow of information among clinicians and support services. Full-time and part-time positions are available. Confidently use Microsoft systems, working with minimal supervision and demonstrating a tactful, sensitive approach to challenging situations. Exhibit empathy and excellent communication skills, acting as the first point of contact by handling telephone calls, emails, and visitors, by responding promptly and efficiently to queries, or redirecting them to the appropriate person/department. Thrive under pressure and prioritise your workload effectively. Collaborate with a large team, demonstrating flexibility in multitasking and covering for colleagues as needed. Communicate effectively with ward teams, matrons, divisional nursing staff, consultants, ward administrators, and patients. Familiarity with the Trust's electronic systems is advantageous but not essential, as training will be provided. Patient Services Administrator We approach our conversations with patients with compassion and respect, recognising that this is a particularly challenging time for them. We seek candidates who are empathetic and capable of handling difficult conversations. If you are resilient and proactive, with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment and respond to urgent requests from our stakeholders while meeting tight deadlines, we want to hear from you. Effective communication with care groups is essential to inform them of any capacity issues or patients at risk of breaching, as well as attending weekly meetings and following the necessary escalation procedures. This role requires close attention to detail and the ability to quickly assimilate information. Full-time and part-time positions are available. The Outpatient Administrator Centre (OAC) staff are dedicated and hardworking, often serving as the first point of contact for patients. Their responsibilities include: Handling approximately 20,000 calls each month from patients. Booking over 650,000 outpatient appointments annually, across 50 specialties within the Trust. Managing clinic schedules, rescheduling, and cancelling appointments, and filling new clinic slots. Covering reception desks at all our locations, checking patients in, scheduling follow-up appointments, and addressing queries. Preparing patient packs for outpatient clinics. Our service operates from 7am to 6pm - Monday to Friday and from 8am to 4:30pm on Saturdays. You will be expected to work flexibly within these core hours. There are roles across the Trust, including in care groups such as Surgery, Outpatient Administration Centre, Pharmacy, Cancer Care and more. Please indicate in your application if there is an area that you would be particularly interested in.
